body:
Devon Ricci: Dr. Whitaker, Alicia, Ron — thanks for joining. Ron, welcome, first time you've been on one of our calls.

Ron Gardner: Yes. I asked James to include me because I'm the one signing the renewal check and I have concerns.

Priya Raman: We want to hear them.

Ron Gardner: Alright. We're eleven months into a two-year contract at four-ninety a year. The pediatric consent routing feature that was supposed to ship in Q1 is now targeting Q3. That was a launch blocker for our pediatric line. So half of what I'm paying for isn't live.

Dr. James Whitaker: To be fair — the adult line has been running well. Containment is at forty-eight percent, our satisfaction scores are up. The technical execution on the adult side is good.

Alicia Park: Compliance-wise, v2 has been solid. BAA is in place, audit logs are working, no incidents.

Ron Gardner: Fine. But that doesn't change the math. We've been running a bake-off against Bland AI for the pediatric line for the last month. Their consent routing is generic but functional. They quoted us three-twenty a year for the pediatric volume alone.

Priya Raman: Ron, let me address this directly. Elena, do you want to speak to where the pediatric feature is?

Elena Sokolova: I'll be straight. We under-scoped it. When we committed to Q1 we hadn't done the design work on the multi-consent flow, and once we started building we discovered we needed to redesign our conversation state model to handle third-party consent transitions cleanly. That work is done as of last week. The pediatric feature is now in QA and will ship July fifteenth.

Dr. James Whitaker: July fifteenth. You're sure?

Elena Sokolova: I'm sure. We have three enterprise customers waiting on this, not just Nimbus. It has the CEO's direct attention.

Ron Gardner: Elena, I appreciate the candor. But candor doesn't fix my P&L for the last six months of paying for an unused feature set.

Priya Raman: Ron, here's what I'm authorized to offer. One, a credit of a hundred and twenty thousand dollars — roughly the pediatric-attributable portion of your fees since January. Two, when the pediatric feature ships in July, we run a joint war-room with your team through go-live at no cost. Three, I extend your contract by six months at no additional fee — so effectively you get eighteen months from now for what remains of the original twenty-four.

Ron Gardner: The credit and the extension are meaningful.

Dr. James Whitaker: Ron, the switching cost to Bland AI on the adult line would be significant. We've built out a whole intent taxonomy and we've integrated with Epic. Moving that is at least four months of work and there's clinical risk in the transition.

Ron Gardner: I know. That's the only reason I'm still at the table. Alicia, what's your read on Bland AI's compliance posture?

Alicia Park: Their BAA is thinner than Voxly's. They subcontract inference to a provider that isn't covered under their BAA the way Voxly's is. That's a real risk.

Ron Gardner: Alright. Here's what I want. The credit. The extension. And I want a written commitment from Elena — signed — that pediatric ships July fifteenth. If it slips again, I want a termination-for-cause clause with prorated refund.

Priya Raman: I can get you all three. Give me until Monday to walk it through our legal team.

Ron Gardner: Monday works.

Dr. James Whitaker: Ron, does this resolve the concern for you?

Ron Gardner: Provisionally, yes. If Elena hits July fifteenth and the war-room support is real, we stay. If either of those falters we revisit.

Devon Ricci: We understand.

Elena Sokolova: Dr. Whitaker, one thing I want to add — I'm personally accountable for the pediatric ship date. I've moved my Q3 planning to make it non-negotiable internally.

Dr. James Whitaker: I appreciate the personal accountability. That matters.

Alicia Park: Elena, one clarifying question — the pediatric consent routing, will it be documented for our security board review?

Elena Sokolova: Yes. Full architectural documentation, threat model, and PHI flow diagram. I'll have a draft to Alicia by June first.

Alicia Park: Perfect.

Ron Gardner: Priya, when you send the amended contract, make sure the termination-for-cause language is explicit. My lawyer is going to redline it and I don't want to iterate three times.

Priya Raman: Understood. I'll have our counsel work with yours directly on that clause.

Ron Gardner: Good.

Dr. James Whitaker: On the Spanish support piece — is that still on track for Q2 or has that slipped too?

Elena Sokolova: Spanish is actually on track. Beta this month, GA September first.

Dr. James Whitaker: That's a positive. We'll want that too.

Devon Ricci: I'll flag Spanish in your account notes so we surface it once GA hits.

Ron Gardner: Alright. We have what we need for now.

Priya Raman: Thank you all. You'll hear from me Monday.

Dr. James Whitaker: Thanks, Priya. Thanks, Devon.

Alicia Park: Thanks all.

Ron Gardner: One more thing — I want a monthly executive check-in until pediatric ships. Thirty minutes, me plus your VP of product.

Elena Sokolova: I'll set that up. Our VP is Priya Kapoor — she'll be on the first call.

Ron Gardner: Perfect.

Devon Ricci: Talk Monday.
